unlisted_practices: Establish a leadership body, such as an FDA sub-committee including physicians, administrators, developers, and investors, to guide generative AI development, validation, and implementation.
Develop guidelines for generative AI model performance, including minimizing hallucination, and for data sharing.
Clarify liability, data privacy, and bias policies for predictive modeling before generative AI insights are put into clinical practice.
The FDA should provide specific regulatory guidance for large language models.
Evaluate generative AI tools at the scale of individual health institutions using a framework such as Wornow et al. so that clinically relevant tools are prioritized.
Create payer incentives and public and private investment to support generative AI implementation in health care.

Use an evaluation checklist for generative AI models applied to EMRs, covering accuracy, hallucination rate, manual correction rate, implementation cost and time, and clinician and patient satisfaction, and run it regularly.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective piece on pathways to implementation for generative AI and LLMs in health care.
